inputs.name: E. coli mu stated, measured; L

day.reading: the 205M is per human lineage (slide gg1@01:26:49; Q14) and G_f is a parallel throughput (slide gg1@01:28:09; Q125)
day.holds: the factor of two and GG-11's 407 treat 205M as a two-lineage total: per lineage 813.5 per generation, 10.6x 76.8 and 21.2x the haploid SNV 38.4; the 38M match is on the diploid 76.8, and on 38.4 the SNV count is 19.35M, 1.81-2.07x short of the 35-40M he cites; the E. coli 22,000 is 2,439 at the measured mu

critic.reading: neutral supply is the null: k = mu, 2 T mu L, with E. coli's supply 93,659x below the human genome's (M-007)
critic.holds: k = mu reproduces exactly (2N mu x 2s/(4Ns) = mu); 76.8 per generation is 107,520x the slide's 180 per 252,000 (53,760x at 38.4); 1,400 is E. coli's throughput and 2,439 its neutral clock; the slide's 205M is bases, not events (M-011), so 407 or 813 per generation is not a point-mutation rate

notes: Rationals for the Taylor identity; floats elsewhere. The Kimura limit is checked numerically at s = 1e-9 and 1e-11 for N = 1e3-1e5. The ancestral-polymorphism remainder (about 15M SNVs) is B5c's R4 B4a and is not recomputed. The fetched caption track differs from the 2026-10-14 copy in recogniser wording only.
